claim: Let \(T\subset\mathbb R^3\) be a regular tetrahedron with vertices \(v_0=0,v_1,v_2,v_3\), edge lattice \(L=\sum_{j=1}^3\mathbb Z v_j\), and reciprocal edge lattice \(L^*=\{\xi:\langle\xi,v_j\rangle\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j=1,2,3\}\). For \(\xi\in L^*\), put \(\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_j=\langle\xi,v_j\rangle\). The Fourier transform of Euclidean surface measure on \(\partial T\) vanishes exactly when the multiset \(\{\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\}\) has multiplicity type \(1+1+1+1\), type \(2+2\), or type \(2+1+1\) with repeated value \(r\) and singleton values \(s,t\) satisfying \(s+t=2r\).
integrity: The infinite classification follows from an exact triangular-face integral and exhaustive multiplicity cases. An included rational-arithmetic finite check is supplementary only and is not used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only the unweighted Euclidean surface measure of a regular tetrahedron on the reciprocal edge lattice. It does not cover volume measure, arbitrary tetrahedra, other polyhedra, or off-lattice frequencies. An equivalent thin-shell diffraction result may exist; one closely related polyhedral-scattering full text was not inspected. No independent audit has been performed.
title: Exact reciprocal-lattice zero classification for a regular tetrahedral shell
